If you only remember one thing today, remember this. Anthropic shipped Fable five point one and cut cache read prices by seventy five percent, on the same day it signed a thirty five billion dollar cloud deal. Frontier capability is going up while the cost of using it goes down. That is the shape of this entire news cycle.

Section one. Anthropic kicks off launch week.

Anthropic released Claude Fable five point one and Mythos five point one on Monday. Same underlying model, two doors. Fable is the generally available version, with production safeguards. Mythos goes to vetted cybersecurity and life sciences organizations, through restricted access.

Base pricing is unchanged. Ten dollars per million input tokens. Fifty per million output. The real move is cache reads. They drop from one dollar to twenty five cents per million. That's a seventy five percent cut. It lands at roughly twenty five percent lower cost for typical workloads.

Your A I News issue from swyx flags the catch. The model produces about seventy percent more output tokens. So some of that saving gets eaten back. Anthropic also signed a thirty five billion dollar cloud deal with Lambda.

Why it matters. When frontier models get cheaper to run over and over, the bottleneck shifts from your budget to what you actually decide to build.

Section two. The video and world model wave.

Two items here, from your Rundown and your A I News. Runway unveiled Solaris. It's calling this the first interface world model. The pitch is a no code internet, where interfaces get generated rather than built.

And Fal's H three Max Live crossed what your A I News issue calls the infinite video generation barrier. You can now produce watchable video faster than you can watch it.

Elsewhere. Amazon shipped its Nova two series, including Nova two Sonic, a native speech to speech model. Google kept pushing its Gemini Flash variants. And Nvidia partnered with MediaTek, to defend its position as big tech firms build their own custom A I chips.

Why it matters. If synthetic video outruns human viewing time, then provenance and verification stop being a nice to have for communications people. They become the job.

Section three. The Pentagon opens the A I front door.

The Department of Defense launched Gen A I dot mil. It's a secure portal, bundling OpenAI's ChatGPT Mil, x A I and Starshield's Grok for Government, and Google Gemini. It's for three million Defense Department personnel. One point seven million unique users are already onboarded.

Why it matters. That is the largest single institutional A I deployment on record. And it happened with almost no public debate about oversight.

Section four. The states are writing the A I rulebook.

While federal action stays at the framework level, state legislatures moved hard this year. Nearly one hundred chatbot specific bills, across thirty four states.

Connecticut passed the session's most comprehensive law. Senate Bill five. It creates a regulatory sandbox, chatbot controls, and a study of independent verification organizations.

But there's a gap. Regulation of automated decision systems has lost momentum. New York's bill and California's bill both stalled, after moving last year. So the systems that decide about hiring, housing and credit are getting less attention than the systems that talk to you.

Why it matters. The rules you will actually have to comply with are being written in Hartford and Sacramento. Not in Washington.

Section five. Chips. The map keeps redrawing.

The compute and transistor density thresholds that trigger U S export licences have been revised downward three times in twenty four months. Since March, chips above certain specifications need notification, even when they're shipped to allied countries.

Meanwhile, demand for A I chips inside China hasn't slowed. It's rerouted. A recent Justice Department indictment laid out how.

Tungsten has emerged as a strategic bottleneck, alongside energy security. And running parallel supply chains for advanced semiconductors adds roughly twenty five to thirty five percent to landed costs.

Why it matters. Export control has stopped being a trade tool. It's become the architecture of two separate tech economies.

Section six. Newsrooms in court.
